answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a oasis as the anchor of the cost.
